title: The Sleepwalkers
subtitle: A Commute to the Museum, and a Night Among the Set

setting.name: Kestrel Avenue North, the Museum of Natural History and the Greensward
setting.description: Days 2 and 3. Forty blocks of the island north of the Library: the long glass canyon of upper Kestrel Avenue, Founders' Circle with its bronze admiral and its subway hub, the west edge of the Greensward with the Merriwick Museum of Natural History on it — a vast Romanesque pile of brownstone halls with a blue whale hanging in its Hall of Ocean Life — and the park itself, where the Kingsgate and Concord river spans now lie across the Great Lawn, perfectly level, with their Day 1 traffic still sitting on them, and where a Lantern has rooted in the Reservoir. Thousands of the Set stand in the Greensward in loose rows below the bridges, each one gently living the moment they were taken. The power fails at noon on Day 2. From then on the city is lit only by the Lanterns.
setting.atmosphere: The scenario of eerie routine. On Day 2 the party discovers that they are not the only people who have worked out the rule, and that the survivors who have worked it out best have turned it into a kind of religion of ordinariness: they commute. At 8:10 every morning and 5:40 every evening, a few hundred people walk the island's avenues with briefcases and coffee cups to jobs that no longer exist, and the Stilts walk among them and do not see them. The Greensward on Day 3 is the most beautiful and terrible place in the campaign: a park full of people who are perfectly content, under two bridges that are lying on the grass, in the light of a thing six hundred feet tall that is humming one note. It should feel like walking through someone else's dream.

keyLocations.name: The 8:10 at Founders' Circle
keyLocations.description: Founders' Circle, at the south-west corner of the Greensward: a great roundabout with a bronze admiral on a column, a subway hub beneath it (four lines, no trains), a bank branch, a Starling's coffee shop and a dozen bus stops. Every morning at 8:10 the Sleepwalkers converge here from all over the Meridian and the Middle Wards, cross the Circle, buy nothing at the shuttered Starling's, and disperse up the avenues to 'work'.
features: Ottilie Branch, seventy-one, with her handbag and her umbrella, walking from the Middle Wards to the First Merriwick branch where she was a teller for forty years
Two Stilts standing at the Circle's north edge, reading the bronze admiral, which they have been doing for a day
The Set: a bus driver at the wheel of a stopped M-7 bus, pulling away from the kerb, over and over; a cyclist at the lights, foot down, waiting
A newsstand with Thursday's papers, which a Set newsagent is still selling, and the Sleepwalkers buy one every day
encounters: A Sleepwalker who breaks (a man who drops his coffee and runs)
secrets: The Sleepwalkers have a second rule the party does not know: the evening pattern is different from the morning one, and at night the only In Pattern places on the island are the places that are busy at night — the theatre district, the all-night delis, the hospital ER bays
Ottilie knows that eleven Sleepwalkers did not come back from the 6:45 ferry 'commute' on Day 2. She thinks they were taken. They were not (see Act 3)

keyLocations.name: The Hall of Ocean Life
keyLocations.description: The Museum of Natural History's great blue hall: a two-storey room the length of a football field, dim, with a ninety-four-foot model blue whale hanging from the ceiling and dioramas of the deep sea around the walls. The Department of Bioacoustics — Yusuf Haddad's lab — opens off its mezzanine. A Stilt has been standing under the whale since Day 1, reading it with its filaments, very slowly, inch by inch.
features: The blue whale, ninety-four feet of fibreglass, and a Stilt beneath it with its threads lifted to the whale's belly as if listening to it
The deep-sea exhibit June's students saw on Thursday: a sound installation of whale song and hydrophone recordings, still playing on a loop on its own battery backup — which is why the Stilt is here
The mezzanine gallery, eighteen feet up, running round the hall; the lab door is at its far end
Emergency lighting, blue, and the sound of the ocean
encounters: Crossing the hall past the Stilt (Act 2)
secrets: The Stilt is not interested in the whale. It is interested in the looping sound installation, which it has been 'reading' for thirty hours. If the installation is turned off, the Stilt will begin to explore the hall, and the museum
Haddad has been living in his lab for two days on vending-machine food, and has crossed the hall four times by walking it as a museum visitor walks it — slowly, stopping at each diorama

keyLocations.name: Yusuf Haddad's Lab
keyLocations.description: A cramped, windowless room off the mezzanine, full of servers, speakers, hydrophone cable, cardboard boxes of tapes and a whiteboard that has been written on, wiped and written on again so many times it is grey. On it, in Haddad's tiny hand: 'THEY ARE NOT SPEAKING. THEY ARE LISTENING.' and, crossed out, 'I asked them.'
features: Nine years of harbor recordings on a server running on a UPS battery with about six hours left
Speakers good enough to play the Visitors' tone back at the volume it arrived
A whiteboard of observations that overlaps with June's notebook to an uncanny degree
A Bluetooth speaker and the first working Lullaby: forty-one seconds of the museum's own lobby on a Tuesday
secrets: 'I asked them' — the playback (see Haddad's companion file). He will not explain it this scenario unless confronted with the whiteboard

The drives Teo carries hold the last three days before the Arrival. On them, at 4:11:52 on Thursday, the Visitors' tone stops being one note and becomes the sound of the city — traffic, ferries, the subway, the Kingsgate Bridge — played back perfectly, as if it had been recorded and was being checked

keyLocations.name: The Great Lawn and the Bridges
keyLocations.description: The heart of the Greensward: fifty-five acres of lawn, now under two bridges. The Kingsgate river span lies east-west across the north half of the lawn, three thousand feet of steel and cable perfectly level on the grass, its towers lying on their sides; the Concord span lies across the south half at an angle. The Day 1 traffic is still on both, and so are many of its drivers, Set. Below and around them, in loose rows, stand the Set — thousands of them, brought here over two days by the Stilts.
features: The Set in their rows: a woman in a green raincoat holding up her phone to film; a man in a suit running on the spot, shouting a name; a cellist in the rows near the bandshell, playing a part from a piece the party will not recognise, without a cello
Pilar Wu, June's student, if she was Lifted in lf-scenario-001: standing near the bridge, mid-stride, running
Officer Paul Castellane, 19th Precinct, in uniform, directing traffic that is not there
Cars on the bridges with their engines still idling on Day 2 and dead on Day 3; car radios playing, then not
Stilts bringing more of the Set across the lawn, slowly, one at a time, all day
secrets: The Set are arranged in rows by the hour they were taken: the 4:12 people nearest the Reservoir, then 4:20, 4:30, outward like tree rings. Investigation DC 14 reveals this. It means the Visitors are filing them
The bridges are not wreckage. Nothing on them is damaged. A Mechanics DC 12 check confirms that the Kingsgate span was lifted off its towers by cutting nothing: the cables simply let go

keyLocations.name: The Reservoir and the Choir
keyLocations.description: The Greensward's great reservoir, a mile around, ringed by a running track and an iron fence. The Lantern stands in the middle of it, rooted in the water: a slow, folded, luminous column six hundred feet tall, the colour of a paper lamp, humming one low note that you feel in your teeth. On the running track on its south shore, twenty people stand in a half-circle with their eyes closed, singing — or holding — a single long chord, in shifts, without stopping. They have been doing it for thirty hours. They call themselves the Choir.
features: The Lantern, and its Dread (WIS save DC 15 within 300 ft)
The Choir: twenty people, led by Noor Abadi, a retired mezzo-soprano, holding one chord in shifts
The Lantern brightens slightly whenever the Choir changes notes, and the Stilts do not touch the Choir at all
A trickle of Choir members who walk, eyes closed, into the Lantern's light at the water's edge, and come back Set
encounters: A Choir member walking into the light
secrets: The Visitors do not Lift the Choir because the Choir is making a pattern — a new one, structured, sustained, and the Lantern is recording it. Noor has discovered something true: the Visitors respond to structure. She has drawn the wrong conclusion: that the Set are going somewhere better
This is the seed of the Performance ending in lf-scenario-004

synopsis: Days 2 and 3. The party leaves the Library at 8 A.M. on Day 2 to take Teo's drives to the scientist they were addressed to — and to look for June's lost student and whoever else is missing — and finds out they are not the only people who know the rule. The Sleepwalkers, a few hundred survivors led in spirit by a seventy-one-year-old bank teller called Ottilie Branch, commute: they walk the avenues at rush hour with briefcases and coffee cups, and the Stilts walk among them blind. The party joins the 8:10, reaches the Museum of Natural History, crosses the Hall of Ocean Life under the nose of a Stilt that has been reading a sound installation for thirty hours, and finds Yusuf Haddad in his lab with nine years of harbor recordings and a working Lullaby. On Day 3 they go into the Greensward, where thousands of the Set stand in rows beneath the two bridges lying on the Great Lawn, and where a Choir holds one chord at the edge of the Reservoir Lantern. They can wake someone — June's student, the woman in the green raincoat, Haddad's partner — and find out what it costs, and that the woken mostly want to go back. The scenario ends on the evening of Day 3 with the crank radio's news that eleven people walked off the 6:45 ferry at Calder Point on Day 2, safe, and a party who now know there is a way across.
hook: The drives in Teo's bag are addressed in a technician's shaking hand to 'Dr. Y. Haddad, Bioacoustics, Merriwick Museum of Natural History — URGENT, HAND DELIVER'. The Museum is forty blocks north on the edge of the Greensward. June knows the building; she was there with her students on Thursday morning. Pilar, if she was Lifted, was carried north toward the park. And at 8:05 on Day 2, from the Library roof, the party sees something that makes the trip possible: dozens of people coming out of doorways all over the Meridian with briefcases and handbags and coffee in paper cups, and walking — not hurrying, not looking up — north up Kestrel Avenue toward Founders' Circle, in the middle of a city of Stilts. One of them, a tiny old woman with an umbrella, looks up at the Library roof as she passes, sees the party, and gives them a small, firm nod, as if to say: well? Are you coming to work or aren't you?

acts.title: Act 1: The 8:10
acts.description: Day 2 morning. The party joins the Sleepwalkers' commute up Kestrel Avenue to Founders' Circle — forty blocks, in pattern, past Stilts — and learns how the Sleepwalkers have survived and what they know. The power fails at noon.
objectives: Decide who stays in the Library and who goes (Peg Odinga will keep the shelter; someone should keep Gerry Voss in hand)
Walk forty blocks In Pattern with the Sleepwalkers
Learn the Sleepwalkers' rules from Ottilie Branch: morning pattern, evening pattern, night places
Reach Founders' Circle and the Museum by noon
encounters: The commute (skill challenge, three Keep Walking checks)
The man who breaks (a Lifting in the middle of the crowd)

scenes.name: Briefcases
scenes.description: The Sleepwalkers walk at commuting pace in loose streams up both sidewalks of Kestrel Avenue. They do not speak above a murmur, they do not look up, they carry things — bags, newspapers, coffee cups, which they refill with water and carry empty. They do not run for lights. The party can join them, and Ottilie Branch will fall into step beside whoever looks most frightened and tell them, in a low, crisp, bank-teller's voice, how it is done.
scenes.readAloud: “They are not hurrying and they are not dawdling. A man in a raincoat with a laptop bag. Two nurses in scrubs. A teenager with earbuds in and nothing coming out of them. A woman pushing an empty stroller. Some of them are carrying coffee cups, and as you fall in among them you realise the cups are empty, and they are carrying them anyway, because that is what you carry at 8:10 on Kestrel Avenue. Ahead of you, at Forty-Eighth, a Stilt is standing in the middle of the avenue with its threads hanging down over the crosswalk like a willow, and the stream of people parts around its legs and closes again on the other side, and nobody looks at it. The tiny old woman with the umbrella falls into step beside you. ‘Eyes on the back of the person in front,’ she says, without turning her head. ‘Think about something dull. Think about your bills. And whatever you do, dear, don’t be late.’”

skillChecks.success: The first ten blocks. The party and its people find the rhythm of the stream.
skillChecks.failure: Someone stops dead at the sight of the Stilt. Ottilie takes their elbow and walks them on, hissing, and the Attention rises by 1.

skillChecks.success: Forty-Eighth Street: through the Stilt's legs. Its threads brush the tops of heads. Nobody looks up.
skillChecks.failure: Someone flinches under the threads. That character is Out of Pattern for a round, and the Stilt turns its whole body toward them — make an immediate second Keep Walking check at DC 15, or be Lifted.

skillChecks.success: The last stretch to Founders' Circle, past the man who breaks (see below), without breaking yourselves.
skillChecks.failure: Your Group loses 1 Calm, and one civilian (GM's choice — not a named one) runs and is Lifted.

skillChecks.success: You notice that the Sleepwalkers who have done this longest walk as if they are actually going somewhere — they have a destination in their heads, a desk, a till — and that it makes them better at it. Thinking of a real destination gives advantage on the next Keep Walking check.
skillChecks.failure: They all look the same: blank, careful, terrified.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene is the payoff for the party's hypothesis: it works, and other people know it works, and it is incredibly frightening to do. Run the three checks as a sequence with growing stakes. Ottilie Branch is the scene's heart: tiny, formidable, widowed, forty years a teller at First Merriwick, and absolutely unwilling to stop going to work. She has been walking to her branch at Founders' Circle every day and sitting at her old window until 5:30.

scenes.name: The Man Who Breaks
scenes.description: At Fifty-Fourth Street a man in the stream drops his cup. It is just a cup. He looks at it on the sidewalk and something goes out of him, and he starts to shout — a name, his wife's — and then to run. The Stilt at the next corner turns.
scenes.readAloud: “It is such a small thing. A paper cup hits the pavement and rolls in a half-circle and stops. The man who dropped it looks down at it for a long moment, and then he looks up, at the sky, at the Lantern over the park, and his face comes apart. ‘Elaine!’ he shouts. ‘ELAINE!’ — and the people around him flinch away from him like he is on fire, and he runs. At the next corner a Stilt that has been standing perfectly still for an hour turns its whole body toward him without seeming to move its legs.”

skillChecks.success: You get to him first and take him down, and hold him still, and put your hand over his mouth, and the Stilt's threads pass over both of you and move on. You have saved a life by tackling a stranger in the street, and you are both Out of Pattern for a round — roll Keep Walking at DC 15 for both of you to get away with it.
skillChecks.failure: He is gone before you can reach him. The stream closes over the place he was. Nobody looks.

skillChecks.success: You get to him with words instead — fast, low, the right thing — and he stops running and stands there shaking, and Ottilie takes his arm, and he walks.
skillChecks.failure: He does not hear you.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Make the players decide, in the moment, whether to break pattern to save someone. It is the dilemma the whole campaign turns on. If they do nothing, Ottilie says quietly afterwards, 'It's all right. You can't. None of us can.' If they do something and survive it, the Sleepwalkers will look at them differently for the rest of the week. His name is Lionel Barre. Elaine is his wife. She is in the Greensward, Set.

scenes.name: Founders' Circle, and Noon
scenes.description: At the Circle the Sleepwalkers disperse to their 'jobs'. Ottilie takes the party into the First Merriwick branch, where she sits at her window and counts nothing, and tells them what the Sleepwalkers know. At noon, mid-sentence, the power fails island-wide: every light, every signal, every alarm, at once.
scenes.readAloud: “The bank is dim and cool and smells of carpet cleaner, and Ottilie Branch sets her handbag on the counter of window three, where it has sat for forty years, and folds her hands on it. ‘Mornings, it’s the walk to work,’ she says. ‘Evenings, it’s the walk home. Night, you stay in, unless you’re somewhere that’s busy at night — the theatres, the hospital, an all-night deli. They know what’s normal for the hour. They know it better than we do.’ She looks at the clock on the wall. ‘That’s running slow. All the clocks are running slow. Have you noticed?’ And then every light in the building goes out, and the traffic light at the Circle outside goes dark, and so does every window up Kestrel Avenue, and for the first time since Thursday the city is perfectly, absolutely silent.”

skillChecks.success: The bank's wall clock, Ottilie's wristwatch, the clock on the Circle's column and the party's phones all disagree with each other — and the mechanical ones are all slow by slightly different amounts. Note it. On Day 6 they will all agree.
skillChecks.failure: Clocks are clocks.

skillChecks.success: Ottilie tells you about the eleven: on Day 2 at 6:30 A.M. a group of Sleepwalkers decided to 'commute' to Calder Point on the 6:45 ferry, as some of them used to, and did not come back. She believes they were taken. (They were not. They are on the mainland.)
skillChecks.failure: She will not talk about the ferry. Her mouth goes thin and she changes the subject.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Ottilie is not a companion NPC, but she is one of the campaign's great minor characters, and the party may want to bring her on the Last Ferry. She will not come until she has 'finished out the week'. The power failure should land hard: from now on, the city's own lights and noises are gone, and the only light at night is the Lanterns.
loot: A First Merriwick branch's emergency kit: 2 flashlights, a first-aid kit, a box of glow sticks (24)
The Sleepwalkers' rules, which are worth more than anything in the vault

acts.title: Act 2: The Hall of Ocean Life
acts.description: Day 2 afternoon and night, in the Museum of Natural History. The party crosses the blue whale hall past the Stilt that is reading the sound installation, finds Yusuf Haddad in his lab, gives him the drives, and listens to the Arrival. Haddad proves the In Pattern rule and introduces the Lullaby. The party spends the night in the museum.
objectives: Get into the Museum and cross the Hall of Ocean Life without being Lifted
Deliver the drives to Dr. Haddad
Listen to the recording of the Arrival and learn what it suggests
Learn the Lullaby, and get Haddad to come with the party
encounters: The Stilt under the whale (evasion; a fight here is Deadly)
A Glitter swarm in the museum's rotunda

scenes.name: Museum Visitors
scenes.description: The museum's west entrance is unlocked (a Set guard holds the door open). The Hall of Ocean Life lies between the rotunda and the stair up to the lab. A Stilt stands under the whale, its threads lifted to the sound installation's speakers in the whale's belly, reading the whale song on its loop. The trick — which Haddad has used four times — is to cross the hall as a museum visitor does: slowly, stopping at each diorama, reading the placards. The hall is three hundred feet long.
scenes.readAloud: “The Hall of Ocean Life is blue and dim and full of the sound of the sea: the installation June’s students sat through on Thursday, whale song and the clicks of dolphins and the long creak of ice, looping on a battery backup in the half-dark. The whale hangs over the whole of it, ninety-four feet long, its belly a great pale curve. And under it, perfectly still, with its long threads lifted up to the whale like a hand raised to touch a ceiling, is a Stilt. It has been here, you will learn, for thirty hours. On the mezzanine above it, at the far end of the hall, a door opens an inch and a man’s face looks out at you, and puts one finger to his lips, and then — very slowly, very deliberately — he walks out onto the gallery and stops in front of the first diorama and reads the placard, and then walks to the next one. He is showing you how.”

skillChecks.skill: Keep Walking (Performance: be a museum visitor)
skillChecks.success: You walk the hall as a Tuesday visitor walks it: stopping, reading, moving on, never hurrying, never looking at the thing under the whale. It does not see you. At the stair, Haddad is waiting, nearly in tears with relief.
skillChecks.failure: You look at it. Just once. You are Out of Pattern for a round and the Stilt lowers its threads from the whale and turns. Make another check at DC 15 or be Lifted; an ally within 5 ft can take your arm and walk you on (advantage).

skillChecks.success: Calla (or someone) takes the mezzanine route — up the service stair, along the gallery rail, never on the floor — and is at the lab door without ever being in the hall at all.
skillChecks.failure: The gallery boards creak. A creak is novel. +1 Attention and the Stilt's threads drift up toward the sound.

skillChecks.success: You realise why it is here: not the whale, but the looping installation. It has been listening to a repeating sound for thirty hours, and it is not bored. It is learning. If you turned the loop off, it would start exploring the museum.
skillChecks.failure: It is under the whale. You do not know why.

combatEncounters.difficulty: Deadly (do not run as a fight)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Stilt is absorbed in the installation and ignores anything In Pattern. It will Lift any creature Out of Pattern within reach (10 ft) and pursue at walking pace anywhere in the hall. It cannot climb to the mezzanine through the gallery rail but can reach anyone on the mezzanine edge (it is 14 ft tall with 10 ft reach). If the installation's loop is switched off, it begins to walk the museum and the whole building is unsafe until a Lullaby is set up. Killing it under the whale is a terrible idea: its falling tone puts the whole Greensward district at Attention 6 for an hour.
combatEncounters.terrain: A long dim hall with dioramas (full cover behind their stone bases), benches, the hanging whale (climbable from the mezzanine, Athletics DC 15), a gallery 18 ft up with a rail.
combatEncounters.statblock: STILT (Large aberration, CR 4). AC 15 (lacquered carapace). HP 68 (8d10+24). Speed 30 ft, climb 20 ft. STR 18 (+4) DEX 12 (+1) CON 16 (+3) INT 14 (+2) WIS 16 (+3) CHA 5 (-3). Saves WIS +5. Skills Perception +7. Resistances piercing, bludgeoning. Vulnerabilities thunder. Condition immunities frightened, charmed. Senses tremorsense 120 ft, blindsight 30 ft; it does not see light at all. Pattern-Blind: it cannot perceive a creature that is In Pattern unless the scene's Attention is 6 or that creature has harmed it. Dread: WIS save DC 12 on first sight (campaign rules). No Anatomy: called shots and Precision Strike-style bonus damage from 'vital spots' do not apply; criticals still double dice. Actions — Multiattack: two Lift attempts, or one Hum. Lift: melee +6 to hit, reach 10 ft, one creature: 2d6+4 bludgeoning (it is not trying to hurt you; that is just what its grip does) and the target is grappled (escape DC 15). On its next turn it carries a grappled creature toward the nearest Lantern at full speed; a creature carried out of sight is gone, and returns Set within the hour. Hum (recharge 5-6): a 30-ft cone of resonance; CON save DC 13, 3d8 thunder damage and Shaken on a failure, half damage and not Shaken on a success. Glass in the cone breaks (+1 Attention). Behaviour: a Stilt walks streets slowly, bending to 'read' anything novel with a fan of fine glassy filaments; it Lifts whatever is Out of Pattern and ignores everything else. It does not pursue into buildings narrower than its 10-ft frame, does not go underground, and if reduced below 20 HP it stops, folds, and gives a long falling tone that sets the Attention in the whole district to 6. Killing one is possible. It is almost always a mistake.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the scenario's set-piece and it is not a fight. It is a walk across a room. Make it last. Describe every diorama they stop at — a giant squid, a coral reef, a whale fall on the abyssal plain with its hagfish and bone-worms — and the Stilt's threads swaying above them. Haddad's demonstration from the gallery is the first time an NPC confirms the rule with his body.

scenes.name: Listening to the Arrival
scenes.description: In the lab, Haddad takes the drives from Teo with both hands, plugs them in and plays the last three days before the Arrival on his speakers. What the party hears is the campaign's central clue. He explains, in hypotheses, what he thinks it means — and his hypothesis is wrong in an interesting way.
scenes.readAloud: “For a long time there is only the harbor: water, the thrum of a ferry’s engines going over, a gull. Then, underneath it, a note. Very low. Patient. It comes from nowhere and it does not change, and it goes on for hours, days — Haddad skips forward, and forward, and it is still there. ‘Nine days,’ he says softly. ‘Nine days I listened to this. Nobody would listen with me.’ Then he skips to the end. Thursday, 4:11 and fifty-two seconds. The note stops. And then the speakers fill with Merriwick: traffic on the Kingsgate Bridge, the subway through the bedrock, the Margaret Duane’s horn, a crowd, a siren, a million small sounds all at once — perfectly clear, perfectly ordinary. ‘That is not the hydrophone,’ Haddad whispers. ‘That is not the harbor. That is them. They are playing it back. They are playing us back to ourselves.’ At 4:12 and nought seconds, the recording ends.”

skillChecks.success: You hear that the playback is perfect — not similar, identical — to sounds from earlier on the same drives. They recorded the city and played it back, checking it. That is not how anything communicates. It is how something copies.
skillChecks.failure: It is beautiful and it is terrifying and you do not know what it means.

skillChecks.success: On the whiteboard, under the eraser-grey, you can make out a line that was wiped off: 'I asked them. I played them the city. 6 days.' Haddad sees you reading it and goes very still. (See his companion file; he will confess if pressed, and the GM truth is that it changed nothing.)
skillChecks.failure: A whiteboard of tiny handwriting.

skillChecks.success: Haddad thinks they are trying to talk. He is wrong, and some part of him knows it, and the part that knows it is frightened.
skillChecks.failure: He is excited. That is all you can tell.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Do not let Haddad lecture. Let him play the recording and let the players draw their own conclusions; then have him offer his hypothesis — 'they are trying to communicate' — and let June, or a player, argue with it. The best outcome is the table arguing about whether this is a conversation or a recording. It is a recording. The question 'what are they recording it for?' is the campaign's back half.
loot: The Arrival recording, on Haddad's laptop

scenes.name: The Lullaby
scenes.description: Haddad shows the party the trick he worked out on Day 1: a looping recording of an ordinary place, played in that place, reads as pattern. He has a forty-one-second loop of the museum lobby on a Tuesday on a Bluetooth speaker, and he wants to test it properly — on the Glitter swarm that has drifted into the rotunda since the power failed — with the party's help.
scenes.readAloud: “‘Forty-one seconds,’ Haddad says, holding up a cheap Bluetooth speaker as if it were a holy relic. ‘The rotunda, last Tuesday, half past two. School groups, a man selling tickets, a child asking about the elephant. Ordinary.’ He presses play. Very softly, the rotunda fills with Tuesday. In the dimness under the dome, a slow drifting cloud of something glittering — it came in an hour ago, after the power failed, and has been hanging over the elephants — pauses. Turns. And drifts away from you, away from the speaker, toward the doors, as if the room had simply become less interesting.”

skillChecks.success: You and Haddad design a real test: play the loop, make a small noise (+1 Attention) beside it, and watch whether the Glitter comes. It does not. Then play it again and again until the Glitter has recorded it twice — and watch it suddenly turn toward the speaker. The Lullaby works, until it is learned. You now understand the rule of the Lullaby in full (see campaignRules).
skillChecks.failure: It works. You do not yet know that it stops working.

skillChecks.success: You can make more: a phone, a recorder, a speaker, ten minutes. Haddad has three speakers to spare.
skillChecks.failure: Haddad has to make them himself, slowly.

enemies: 1 Glitter swarm (only if the test goes wrong)
combatEncounters.tactics: If the Lullaby has been 'learned' and nobody notices, the swarm descends on the speaker and anyone near it and uses Static. A fire extinguisher or a burning brochure disperses it.
combatEncounters.terrain: The museum rotunda: a marble floor under a dome, a herd of stuffed elephants on a plinth (full cover).
combatEncounters.statblock: GLITTER (Medium swarm of Tiny aberrations, CR 1). AC 12. HP 22 (5d8). Speed 0 ft, fly 30 ft (hover). STR 3 (-4) DEX 15 (+2) CON 10 (+0) INT 1 (-5) WIS 12 (+1) CHA 1 (-5). Resistances bludgeoning, piercing, slashing. Immunities grappled, paralyzed, prone, restrained, frightened. Senses blindsight 60 ft. Swarm: it can occupy another creature's space and move through openings an inch wide; it cannot regain HP. Record: the Glitter remembers every sound made within 30 ft of it. It replays them later, elsewhere, at random — a dead man's voice, the party's names, a gunshot — and each replay in a scene is +1 Attention. Harmless in Pattern: a Glitter swarm does not attack anything unless it is struck, sprayed, burned or shouted at from inside it. Actions — Static: every creature in the swarm's space makes a CON save DC 12, 2d6 lightning damage on a failure, half on a success (1d6 if the swarm is at half HP or less). Behaviour: drifts like dust in a sunbeam, towards novelty. It is the Visitors' ears. Fire disperses it (a burning swarm takes double damage), and a fire extinguisher's cone deals it 2d6 cold.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The Lullaby is the party's first tool, and it should feel like one: a small, cheap, clever thing that works. Make sure they also learn its limit (it stops working once it has been recorded twice), so that they keep needing to make new ones. Haddad will come with the party from here, if asked, because the drives were the last thing his technician did and the party carried them.
loot: Three Bluetooth speakers (about 6 hours each) and the museum-lobby Lullaby

acts.title: Act 3: The Greensward
acts.description: Day 3. Into the park: the Set in their rows under the two bridges, a waking, the Choir at the Reservoir, and Ushers in the woods of the Tangle on the way out. The party returns to the Library — or wherever they are sheltering — at dusk to hear the radio report of the eleven who came off the ferry.
objectives: Walk among the Set and find someone: Pilar Wu, the woman in the green raincoat, Lionel Barre's wife Elaine, Haddad's partner Hal
Wake someone, and learn what it costs
Meet the Choir and understand what Noor Abadi has found
Get back out of the park through the Tangle at dusk
encounters: Four Ushers in the Tangle (Hard for level 2; evasion preferred)
A Choir member walking into the Lantern's light

scenes.name: The Rows
scenes.description: The Set stand in loose rows across the Great Lawn under the bridges. They are warm, breathing and calm. If touched they do not react; if moved more than a few feet they drift gently back. Stilts bring more of them across the grass all day, slowly. The party can walk among them freely — the rows are, in a sense, the most In Pattern place on the island — but the Lantern is three hundred yards away across the Reservoir and Dread applies.
scenes.readAloud: “The Kingsgate Bridge is lying on the grass. You have driven over it, or under it, or looked at it from a window every day of your life, and it is lying on the Great Lawn like a toy, perfectly level, its cables slack, its towers on their sides, three thousand feet of it, with cars still on it — a yellow cab, a delivery van, a minivan with a stick-figure family on the back window. And below it, among it, around it, in long loose rows like a crop, the people. Thousands of them. A man in a suit running on the spot, mouth open. A woman lifting a phone up at nothing. Two teenagers holding hands, laughing at something one of them said four days ago. A cellist with no cello, bowing the air, eyes closed. Nobody is hurt. Nobody is afraid. It is very quiet, except for the Lantern’s note, and a soft, continuous, overlapping murmur — thousands of people saying the last thing they said.”

skillChecks.success: The rows are arranged by time: the 4:12 people nearest the Reservoir, then later ones outward, like tree rings. The Visitors are filing them. Haddad goes pale.
skillChecks.failure: Rows. Thousands of them. It is hard to look for one face.

skillChecks.success: You find who you came for (Pilar is in the 4:50 rows, still running; the woman in the green raincoat is in the 4:31 rows, filming; Elaine Barre is in the 5:00 rows; Officer Paul Castellane is in the 4:20 rows, directing traffic; the cellist is Hal).
skillChecks.failure: An hour of searching. Then you find them anyway — but it is now the afternoon, and dusk in the Tangle is coming.

skillChecks.success: Abena examines one: pulse 64, resps 12, pupils reactive, blood sugar normal, no dehydration after three days without water. They are not starving. They are not anything. Whatever is keeping them is keeping them perfectly.
skillChecks.failure: They are alive. That is all you can say.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Let the players wander. Every Set person is a one-line story, and the GM should improvise a dozen: a man proposing on one knee; a delivery rider looking at his phone; a woman yelling at a parking warden, both of them Set, forever. Do not rush to the waking. The horror here is that it is not horrible.

scenes.name: Waking
scenes.description: Someone who knows a Set person says their name and something true they have never heard. CHA (Persuasion) DC 15 (advantage for family or a lover). June can wake Pilar ('Pilar. You were right about the titration. I marked it wrong. I'm sorry.'); Calla can wake the woman in the green raincoat only with a confession ('It was me. I set the alarm.') and a stranger's name she has to learn from the woman's phone lock-screen; Haddad can wake Hal; Lionel Barre, if he survived Act 1, can wake Elaine. The woken person drops to the grass, is Shaken for a day, and counts as Out of Pattern for an hour — which, three hundred yards from the Lantern, is a problem.
scenes.readAloud: “For a long moment nothing happens. Then the person in front of you stops — just stops, in the middle of the thing they have been doing for three days — and the light goes out of their face and something else comes into it, and they look at you. Really look. ‘What,’ they say. ‘What — where — what time is it?’ And then their legs go, and they sit down hard on the grass, and somewhere across the Reservoir, the Lantern’s note changes, very slightly, as if something six hundred feet tall had turned its head.”

skillChecks.success: They wake. Now get them out: they are Out of Pattern for an hour and the Attention in the Greensward rises by 2 at once.
skillChecks.failure: They do not hear you. You may try once more, with something truer. A third failure means they cannot be woken by you.

skillChecks.success: You get the woken person off the lawn and into the trees, walking them, holding them up, murmuring. The Lantern's light passes over the lawn behind you and does not find you.
skillChecks.failure: The Lantern turns. Within 1d4 rounds its light sweeps the rows. Anyone Out of Pattern in the open is Lifted unless they reach cover or get back into pattern (another check). The woken person, if not covered, is Set again.

skillChecks.success: Once they are safe, you see it: they want to go back. Pilar says she was running to catch the train and she knew she was going to make it and it was the best feeling. Hal says the second movement had never gone so well. Most of the woken will ask, quietly, if they can go back.
skillChecks.failure: They are crying. You assume it is relief.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the emotional centre of the scenario and the campaign's first moral question: is waking someone a rescue? Let the woken argue. Hal will walk back into the rows the next morning if Haddad does not stop him, and Haddad will have to decide whether to. Pilar will stay woken if June asks her to. The woman in the green raincoat — Danielle Okafor-Reyes, a paralegal — will want to know who set off the alarm, and Calla will have to decide whether to tell her.

scenes.name: The Choir
scenes.description: On the Reservoir's south running track, twenty people in a half-circle hold one long chord, in shifts, eyes closed. The Stilts walk around them. The Lantern brightens when they change notes. Noor Abadi, fifty-eight, a retired mezzo-soprano from the Merriwick Opera, leads them and believes the Set are going somewhere better. While the party watches, one of the Choir — a young man, Theo — walks into the light at the water's edge, eyes closed, still singing, and comes back Set.
scenes.readAloud: “You hear them before you see them, a sound under the Lantern’s note like a cello under an organ: twenty voices holding one chord, not quite in tune, not stopping. They stand on the running track in a ragged half-circle with their eyes shut, swaying very slightly, breathing in shifts so the sound never breaks. A Stilt walks behind them along the fence, its threads drifting over their heads, and does not touch them. When the woman in the middle — sixty, silver hair, a voice like a dark room — opens her mouth wider and lets the chord climb one step, the Lantern above the water brightens, very slightly, as if listening. A young man at the end of the line opens his eyes and smiles at you, and then turns, and walks down the bank and into the light at the water’s edge, still singing.”

skillChecks.success: You join the chord for a breath, and you feel it: the Lantern's attention on you, enormous, not hostile, interested. It is the first time anyone in the party has been looked at by a Visitor and not Lifted. You understand that the Choir is not hiding. It is being heard.
skillChecks.failure: Your voice is the wrong note. The Choir flinches. +1 Attention.

skillChecks.success: Noor talks to you after her shift. She believes the Visitors are taking the Set somewhere better and that the Choir will go with them. She also tells you what she has found: they do not Lift what is structured. 'They are collectors,' she says. 'Of patterns. We are giving them a new one.' (She is right about that, and wrong about the rest.)
skillChecks.failure: She does not stop singing to speak to people who are not singing.

skillChecks.success: You catch Theo at the water's edge and pull him back before the light takes him. He is furious, and Out of Pattern, and the Lantern turns.
skillChecks.failure: He is gone into the light.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Noor is a seed for lf-scenario-004, where a sustained, structured performance at the Harbor Lantern can hold its attention while the Last Ferry crosses — at the cost of the performer. Plant it here: the Choir is not Lifted, and the Lantern brightens when they change. Do not let the players turn the Choir into a solution yet; they do not know enough.

scenes.name: The Tangle at Dusk
scenes.description: The way back out of the park, west to the Museum or south to Founders' Circle, runs through the Tangle — thirty-eight acres of dense woods, rock outcrops, stone bridges and winding paths in the middle of the Greensward. At dusk on Day 3, four Ushers are working the Tangle, herding deer, raccoons and the occasional human toward the Reservoir. A woken person is with the party, and they are Out of Pattern.
scenes.readAloud: “It is getting dark in the Tangle and the paths are not where you remember them. The trees are close and the rocks are wet and every step on the leaf litter sounds like a gunshot. Somewhere ahead and to the left there is a sound like a fingertip run around the rim of a glass, and then, to the right, another one answering. A deer bolts across the path in front of you, white tail up, and something low and glittering goes after it in one bound, and then another, and you hear the deer stop being a deer somewhere in the dark. The woken person beside you is breathing too fast.”

skillChecks.success: Teo's Trailwise finds the line: a rocky path along the Tangle's west edge where the leaf litter is thin. Advantage on Stealth for the party.
skillChecks.failure: You are on the main path, in the open, with leaves underfoot.

skillChecks.success: You get through the Tangle without the Ushers feeling you. Freeze when they come close; they circle and move on.
skillChecks.failure: An Usher feels the woken person's footsteps. It Chimes. Combat.

combatEncounters.tactics: They come at whoever is moving fastest — the woken person, almost certainly — and try to Herd them east toward the Reservoir. They work in pairs, one Herding and one Nipping anyone who interferes. If nothing moves more than 10 ft for a full round, they lose track and circle. Gunfire is +3 Attention and at Attention 6 a Stilt arrives from the Great Lawn in 1d4 rounds. A party that fights all four in the open will win, hurt, and be hunted out of the park; a party that freezes, uses a Lullaby or gets onto the stone bridge over the Gill (the Ushers will not cross running water more than knee deep) gets out clean.
combatEncounters.terrain: Dense woods (half cover everywhere), rock outcrops (full cover, climbable DC 12), a stone footbridge over a stream called the Gill (Ushers will not wade it), leaf litter (disadvantage on Stealth on the main paths).
combatEncounters.statblock: USHER (Medium aberration, CR 2). AC 14 (folded glass plates). HP 33 (6d8+6). Speed 50 ft. STR 14 (+2) DEX 18 (+4) CON 12 (+1) INT 6 (-2) WIS 14 (+2) CHA 3 (-4). Skills Perception +4, Stealth +6. Resistances piercing. Senses tremorsense 60 ft. Pattern-Blind (as Stilt). Herding: it has advantage on attack rolls and shoves against any creature that moved more than 10 ft on its last turn — running is the thing it hunts. Stillness: an Usher that cannot perceive movement in a creature for a full round (the creature took no move and no action except Keep Walking or Dodge) loses track of it and circles. Actions — Nip: melee +6 to hit, 1d8+4 piercing. Herd: the Usher shoves a creature up to 10 ft in a direction of its choice (contest: its Athletics +2 with advantage from Herding if applicable, against the target's Athletics or Acrobatics); used to push people toward a Stilt or a Lantern. Bonus action — Chime: it rings like a struck glass; every Usher within 300 ft knows where it is (+1 Attention). Behaviour: Ushers come in twos and fours and work like sheepdogs, not wolves. They want to drive runners toward a Stilt to be Lifted. They bite only what resists. They break off when nothing in the scene is moving fast.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The scenario's only real fight, and it is optional. It is the first time the party protects someone who is a magnet for the Visitors, and it is a dress rehearsal for the Last Ferry. If they get out clean using what they have learned (stillness, the Gill, a Lullaby), say so: 'You did that right.'

scenes.name: Eleven
scenes.description: Back at the Library (or the museum) on the evening of Day 3, the crank radio has a new story: on Day 2, at 7:12 A.M., the Margaret Duane docked at Calder Point on the mainland and eleven people walked off her — calmly, with briefcases, in single file — and walked through the terminal and out into the arms of the National Guard. They were Ottilie's eleven Sleepwalkers. They are fine. They are being 'debriefed'. Nobody on the mainland has worked out what they did right.
scenes.readAloud: “‘…the eleven individuals, who walked off the Pier Point ferry at seven-twelve yesterday morning, are reported to be in good health and are being interviewed by federal authorities. Witnesses at Calder Point described them as calm. One witness said they appeared to be going to work.’ Peg Odinga turns the crank a few more times so the radio does not fade. Nobody in the reading room says anything. Then Ottilie Branch — if she is here — sets down her teacup, very precisely, in its saucer. ‘Well,’ she says. ‘Well. There you are.’”
scenes.roleplayNotes: End here. The ferry works, if you take it the right way. The players will want to go tomorrow. The next scenario shows them why it is not that simple: on Day 4 at 8:15, three hundred people who heard the same broadcast rush the boat. Level up: the party reaches level 3.

npcsInvolved.name: Yusuf Haddad, 44
npcsInvolved.description: The scientist the drives were addressed to. Has been living in his lab for two days and has worked out the Lullaby. Joins the party here. See his companion file.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Understand them; find Hal; be forgiven for the playback.

npcsInvolved.name: Ottilie Branch, 71
npcsInvolved.role: Sleepwalker / the island's most formidable commuter
npcsInvolved.description: Forty years a teller at First Merriwick, Founders' Circle branch; widowed; tiny; walks to work every day of the Arrival with her handbag and umbrella and sits at window three until 5:30. Knows the morning, evening and night patterns better than anyone.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To finish out the week. She is not afraid of dying; she is afraid of being late. She will get on the Last Ferry only if someone convinces her it is a commute.

npcsInvolved.name: Noor Abadi, 58
npcsInvolved.description: Retired mezzo-soprano of the Merriwick Opera, silver-haired, magnetic, gentle, certain. Her Choir has held one chord at the Reservoir for thirty hours and the Visitors do not touch it.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To be taken with the Set to wherever they are going, and to bring as many people as want to come. She is the person who can perform for the Harbor Lantern in lf-scenario-004 — and she will want to.

npcsInvolved.name: Lionel Barre, 52
npcsInvolved.description: An insurance assessor who has walked with the Sleepwalkers for a day without speaking, and breaks on Fifty-Fourth Street when he drops his cup. His wife Elaine is in the 5:00 rows on the Great Lawn.

npcsInvolved.name: Hal Okonedo, 46
npcsInvolved.description: Principal cello of the Merriwick Chamber Orchestra, Set in the rows near the bandshell, bowing the air. Wakeable by Haddad. Woken, he wants to go back.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The second movement, which had never gone so well.

npcsInvolved.name: Pilar Wu, 16
npcsInvolved.description: Quiet, fast, clever, was running for the subway when she was Lifted. Set in the 4:50 rows, still running.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Woken, she wants her mother. She stays woken if June asks.

npcsInvolved.name: Danielle Okafor-Reyes, 34
npcsInvolved.role: The woman in the green raincoat
npcsInvolved.description: A paralegal who stopped on Forty-Third Street to film a car alarm. Set, still filming. Woken, she wants to know who set the alarm off.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get home to her daughter in Ashford, across the Tidewater, where the Kingsgate Bridge used to land.

rewards.money: $0 that matters. Cash is now worthless on the island; nobody is selling anything. The First Merriwick branch vault holds about $340,000, and Ottilie Branch will not let anyone touch it.
items: Three Bluetooth speakers and the museum-lobby Lullaby (about 6 hours of battery each)
Haddad's laptop with the Arrival recording and nine years of harbor sound
A First Merriwick emergency kit: 2 flashlights, a first-aid kit, 24 glow sticks
The Sleepwalkers' rules: morning, evening and night patterns
Whoever the party woke, and the knowledge of what waking costs
The radio report: eleven people walked off the 6:45 ferry at Calder Point
rewards.story: The party ends Day 3 knowing the rule for certain, owning a tool (the Lullaby), and having seen the Set and the Choir. They know the ferry can cross. They do not know that by tomorrow morning everyone else will know it too. The xp figure is per character: it takes each from level 2 to level 3.

twists: The Set are not suffering. Most of the woken want to go back. Hal is the clearest case; let him be gentle and certain and heartbreaking about it.
The Sleepwalkers' eleven 'taken' on the 6:45 ferry were not taken. They crossed. The ferry is a way off — if you board it like a commuter.
The rows are arranged by time. The Visitors are not collecting people; they are filing a moment, and people are in it.
Noor's Choir is not Lifted because it is making a structured pattern the Visitors are recording. She thinks it is a prayer being answered. It is a library acquiring a new book.
dmTips: THE COMMUTE IS THE SCENARIO. Run Act 1 slowly and specifically, with the Stilt's threads over people's heads. It should be the most frightening walk of the players' lives and it should work.

HADDAD IS A HYPOTHESIS MACHINE, NOT AN ANSWER MACHINE. In this scenario he believes the Visitors are communicating; the players should be the ones to push him to 'recording'. When they do, let him light up.

WAKING IS A CHOICE WITH A PRICE. The Attention spike at the waking is real, and the Lantern turning is the scenario's best moment of terror. And the woken person's wish to go back is its best moment of grief. Do not resolve either for the players.

THE CHOIR IS A SEED. Do not let the players solve the campaign with Noor now. If they try a Performance at the Reservoir Lantern, it holds the Lantern's attention for as long as the performance lasts and costs nothing yet — but there is no ferry to cross under it. Note that it works, and wait.

ABENA'S HOSPITAL. If Abena's player insists on going to Mercy Eastgate on Day 2 or 3, let them: it is two miles east across the Greensward's south end, the ER bays are In Pattern at night (they are always busy at night), and nine ventilated patients are on Unit 4 with three nurses who will not leave them and a generator with fuel for four days. Make it a sidebar of one or two scenes and seed lf-scenario-004's gathering. The patients cannot be moved in pattern without a plan; that is the point.

THE POWER FAILS AT NOON ON DAY 2. From then on the nights are black except for the Lanterns. Use it. The party's flashlights are Out of Pattern at night anywhere a flashlight would be unusual — which is everywhere.
LEVEL UP AT 'ELEVEN'. The party reaches level 3 at the end of Day 3.
